The continuous function $P(t)$ shows the rate at which people walk into a store at time $t$ hours. There were $15$ people present in the store at time $t = 0$. The values for $P(t)$ are given in the table below.

| $t(hours)$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ | $7$ | $10$ | $13$ | $16$ | $18$ | $20$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $P(people/hour)$ | $15$ | $10$ | $7$ | $15$ | $20$ | $35$ | $45$ | $50$ | $60$ |

Use the midpoint Riemann sum with the partitions
$[0, 4], [4, 10], [10, 16], [16, 20]$
to approximate the total number of people that have walked into the store by time $t = 20$.

> A calculator is required to answer this question.

The following table shows the rate $r(t)$, in popcorn kernels per second, at which a machine makes popcorn over a period of $60$ seconds.

| $t(seconds)$ | $0$ | $15$ | $30$ | $45$ | $60$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $r(popcorn kernels/second)$ | $20$ | $40$ | $50$ | $60$ | $40$ |

Use the midpoint Riemann sum for $r(t)$ over the interval $[0, 60]$ with two equal subintervals to approximate the number of corn kernels popped by the machine in one minute.

> A calculator is required to answer this question.
